correctness.rationale: A side with at least three white vertices cannot have a first force into that side, and equal white two-sets prevent any first force. If a side has two whites, a blue vertex with index in that two-set but not in the opposite white set can force, reducing the count. For two singleton white sets an index outside their union is available since n≥3. Counting by number omitted gives the five stated coefficients; each white singleton has at least two two-set extensions, so every feasible pair extends to distinct white two-sets, proving equicardinality. Centering at x=−n/2 gives the stated biquadratic with squared roots −n(n−2)/4 ± √(n(n−1)/2). They are distinct and nonzero; the larger is negative for n≥5 (n(n−2)^2−8(n−1)>0 at n=5 and increasing), and positive at n=3,4. Positive quartic coefficients exclude nonnegative real roots. The constant term of the quartic is positive, so the zero multiplicity is exactly 2n−4. The supplied verification_output.txt is consistent with the proof; its subset and shift tests are finite, and the uploaded code was not run.
